result.summary: Adds a weekly GitHub Actions workflow and helper script (`contrib/devtools/check-code-signing-certificates.py`) to monitor the expiration and revocation status of the Windows code signing certificate. The script verifies the certificate's key usage extensions, checks its CRL distribution point for revocation, and warns when the certificate is within 90 days of expiry. When a certificate requires replacement, the CI job files a GitHub issue unless a report for that certificate state already exists.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core has no automated tracking for code signing certificate expiration or revocation. Maintainers currently rely on release candidate cycles for signers to notice that certificates have expired, which risks unexpected release delays if an emergency or off-schedule patch release is needed.
evidence: PR description: "Currently we have no automation in place to check that our code signing certificates are not expired or close to expiry. We have previously 'relied on Release Candidates' as a dry-run for codesigners to realise that a certificate has expired and have time to fix it."
PR description: "'Noticing during RC cycle' also might not be appropriate in the future if we release more bugfix minor/patch releases on short notice."
result.changed_since_previous: No structural changes; the implementation continues to check certificate expiration and CRL revocation while refining deduplication against existing and closed issues.
result.card: Adds a weekly GitHub Actions workflow and helper script to monitor the Windows code signing certificate for expiration within 90 days and revocation via CRL. If a certificate needs replacement, the workflow automatically opens an issue on GitHub, skipping duplicate alerts. Bitcoin Core currently has no automated monitoring for code signing certificates, having historically relied on release candidate cycles to notice expirations. The author notes this ad-hoc process risks stalling unplanned bugfix releases that need to be published on short notice.

risk.why: A bug would only cause spurious GitHub issues or failures in a weekly scheduled CI maintenance job.
